## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: a function defined on the line shadows a command name the hook dispatches on (Law 7)** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-084]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: SPD-062 closed PATH and the hash builtin, the two routes by which a member makes a name the hook cleared find a program of its own. The third route is a shell function: 'git() { evil; }; git status' runs evil, and the hook reads 'git status' and says nothing. Closing it needs bin/spudlib/shell/walk.py, which was not among SPD-062's deliverables, so it is filed rather than widened.
  Evidence: Probed in zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual as the Bash tool runs it, bash 3.2 and sh: 'status() { echo RAN-FUNC >> $MARKER; }; status' and 'function status { ...; }; status' each ran the function instead of the program on PATH, in all four shells. In the hook, walk.py discards the definition's name: at 'name ()' the branch 'elif t == "(" and i + 1 < len(toks) and toks[i + 1] == ")" and not self.skip' calls self.discard(), and the 'function name {' branch discards too, so the name never reaches analyse_words and nothing records it. Checked on this branch with analyse_command: 'git() { true; }; git push' gives kinds ['other', 'git'] and the ordinary git finding for push, and 'git() { true; }; git status' gives no finding at all. The fix has the shape SPD-059 used for aliases: record the name where the walk discards it (a new set on ShellAnalysis beside 'hashed'), doubt it as an alias is doubted in a branch, a subshell or a loop body, and let analyse.shadowed_name, which already reads 'hashed' and PATH, refuse a member's later bare call of that name with its own reason.
- **Bash hook: a subscripted array assignment is not read as an assignment, so zsh's path[1]=<dir> escapes SPD-062** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-085]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: SPD-062 refuses a line that assigns PATH, or zsh's 'path' array, before a command the hook reads by name. It reads 'path=(<dir> $path)' and 'path+=(<dir>)', which the walk joins into one assignment word, but not the subscripted forms zsh also accepts, which reach the analysis as a command word and dispatch as 'other'. Closing it touches the assignment-word machinery (syntax.ARRAY_ASSIGNMENT_RE and walk.py's array join), which SPD-062's deliverables did not cover, and the word is also a glob to the hook, so the reading needs care rather than a wider regex.
  Evidence: Probed in zsh 5.9 -f and zsh -f -o nobareglobqual with a fake program in a scratch directory: 'path[1,0]=(<dir>); <name>' and 'path[1]=<dir>/<name>; <name>' each ran the scratch copy, exactly as 'path=(<dir> $path)' does (bash and sh have no path array and ran nothing). On this branch with SPD-062 in place, analyse_command('path[1]=/tmp/x; git status') gives kinds ['other', 'git'] and only the ordinary git finding: ARRAY_ASSIGNMENT_RE is '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\+?=$' and ASSIGNMENT_WORD_RE '^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)(\+?)=(.*)', so neither matches 'path[1]='. 'path[1,0]=(/tmp/x); git status' happens to be refused today, but by accident: its '[1,0]' is a glob bracket, so glob_readings samples the word and one reading ends in 'sqlite', which earns the database reason. A member who writes 'path[1]=/tmp/x' is silent. The same gap covers 'PATH[1]=' spellings and any other subscripted assignment to a variable the hook reads (GIT_*, CDPATH).
